threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think it's weird when a shop closes at 5 PM, while the pub stays open till midnight. Welcome to Dalston, mate!
Last night on the 59, a bloke in a panda onesie serenaded the driver with a guitar. Only in Brixton, right?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw the local kids setting up a street festival with makeshift stalls and thrifted decorations—there's creativity in chaos that only feels like home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg can you grab a döner at 2 AM, then debate art with a street musician while the U-Bahn is on strike. It's a vibe like no other.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local when they happily dodge the BART delays but still know the best taco spot within a two-block radius.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in full clown makeup on the 6 bus, juggling oranges while explaining his philosophy on happiness. Only in SF.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all hip bars and trendy shops. They miss the quiet corners where old ladies gossip over café amb llet.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can spot them by the way they struggle to find the right 'tapa' at the bar, still asking for 'tapas' like it’s a buffet.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still think the local corner shop accepts card payments. Good luck with that when the cash-only queues start.
Saw a bloke in a suit on the 277 last night, loudly debating the ethics of pineapple on pizza. Had the whole back row in stitches.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The smell of fresh falafel wafting through the streets on a Saturday evening, mixed with the laughter from families at the parks. That’s when it hit me.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Kreuzberg do you find a late-night Späti selling fresh currywurst, but only if you order it in German. It’s a culinary rite of passage.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by their instinct to avoid any BART delays. They know the best taco trucks to hit during rush hour instead.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Caught the 47 bus today—driver had his playlist blasting 90s hip-hop. Passengers were dancing in the aisles like it was a nightclub on wheels.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think the best tapas are at fancy places, but the hidden gems are in the tiny bars where the old locals gather over vermut.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by the way they still check their Google Maps for a street that’s been there for decades. A true Gràcia local knows the shortcuts.
